items.summary: Prefer spoken contractions such as I'll, don't, can't, and won't over I will, I do not, cannot, and will not when the boundary remains clear.
Use Sure, Of course, All right, or Okay instead of Confirmed and Understood when the customer-facing moment is not formal.
Voicemail should usually trigger logging and retry behavior, not spoken content to the mailbox.
Support and cancellation routes should be short because the customer is no longer in a sales conversation.
Small modal words change meaning. Use can't for medical advice inability, and avoid too much certainty in security/compliance routes.
Coverage facts from an approved policy document may be answerable knowledge, while recommendations or advice still need a qualified reviewer.
When the customer asks for a callback, answer briefly and ask for a time instead of giving a reassurance paragraph.
For autonomy concerns, a small mirror such as no rush can make the answer sound more human when it does useful work.
